Over millions of years you grow to realize your dream: to harbor life on beautiful landscapes. Players take turns drafting land tokens choosing where to put it on their planet board. By completing one of the pattern available before the others, they can claim the corresponding biome card and have life appears on their planet. The winner is the player with the most points from biome cards and moon bonus points. In case of a tie, the planet with the most different types of terrain is the winner. Number of players: 2 - 4 Game duration: 11 mn Complexity: 2 / 5 Play Biomos and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Moon 4 End game Overview Complete your planet and nearby moon with tokens Turn First, take a terrain token from the pool (If the pool is empty, refill it to 5) Place the chosen token onto your Planet board in any empty space (you can always make space by sliding previous tokens, but cannot rearrange tokens already placed) If you match a sequence as shown on a Biome card, you may claim it. However, you can only claim ONE biome per turn, even if you match several. Moon Your moon space, in the corner, is a special space that can only hold one token and can never be changed once filled It can be filled as you normally would any other empty space At the point of making your moon, you MAY move a token on your planet to a different position At end game, your moon gives you 3 points per matching token in your planet (The moon itself is NOT scored) End game The game ends when all players have filled their planet and moon with tokens Score all biomes collected during the game Score 3 bonus points per planet token which matches your moon token The player with the most points wins! If tied, the player with the most varied tokens wins! [Rating: 1/10] They left a 12 point card out of the card as a promo and refuse to sell it to customers of their games. Stop alienating customers that can’t make it to a convention and just give them the pickle, or make an extra buck by selling it to them for $3 to $5.

[Rating: 2/10] So basic that it leaned towards boring for us. There's nothing technically wrong with it, but I have no interest in playing again.

[Rating: 3/10] Une seule partie plate et ennuyeuse, en mode expert. On est dans le même registre que Valbara, mais ce dernier (sans être sensationnel) est beaucoup plus fluide et moins tarabiscoté. La forme (originale) est clairement meilleure que le fond.

[Rating: 3/10] Random with open drafting pool created from drawing out of the bag and the objectives are randomly drawn.  Sometimes one is out there and you already have it and other times it is not close at all to the objective. Art is nice but generic.  No theme. No need to own.

[Rating: 3/10] Played this a lot with a friend online who really liked it, I found it utterly boring, but you know I was playing a game with my friend so no big deal!

[Rating: 3.2/10] Méchanique interessante de draft de biomes qui sont intercalables. Mais l'absese dramatique d'interet des objectifs et le cot aléatoire très fort noient le plaisir.
